title: Eigenstate thermalization at the edge of the many-body spectrum
authors: Arnav Pushkar, Pranay Patil, Soumya Bera, Masaki Tezuka, Sumiran Pujari
abstract: It is well-known that thermalization breaks down in presence of an extensive number of symmetries or conservation laws that are mutually compatible or commuting with each other. We ask here how an extensive number of mutually incompatible local symmetries govern eigenstate thermalization (ETH). We will investigate this through models within the class of bond-dependent $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric quantum spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Hamiltonians that naturally admit this structure. This leads to exponentially large degeneracies in the spectrum governed by the incompatible symmetry structure. Here, using spectral diagnostics, we show that non-integrability can survive despite extensively many conserved quantities when they are incompatible. Furthermore, we show that ETH behavior persists deep into the many-body spectral edge due to this structure. In other words, incompatible local symmetries enable a mechanism to obtain enough thermodynamic entropy at low excitation energy densities to make ETH operational or predictive near the ground state.
summary: This work explores Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) in quantum spin systems with extensive, incompatible symmetries. By analyzing 1D and 2D spin models, the authors show that these symmetries do not necessarily destroy thermalization. They demonstrate that ETH persists robustly near the spectral edge, suggesting a mechanism for achieving thermodynamic behavior even with minimal excitation energy.
main_problem: The paper investigates the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) in quantum systems possessing an extensive number of mutually incompatible local symmetries (EMICQ). It specifically addresses whether ETH remains valid near the spectral edge despite these symmetries.
main_result: The study demonstrates that incompatible local symmetries allow non-integrability to persist and enable ETH behavior to remain operational deep into the many-body spectral edge, even with minimal excitation energy.
method: The authors use spectral diagnostics, analyzing the average gap ratio, entanglement entropy scaling, and fluctuations of local observables across different energy windows.
model_or_system: The models studied are bond-dependent Z2-symmetric quantum spin-1/2 Hamiltonians, including a 2D checkerboard model and a 1D chain. These models are engineered to exhibit the EMICQ structure.
key_observables: Mean Entanglement Entropy (EE), average gap ratio $\langle r angle$, fluctuations of local observable matrix elements ($	ext{Dm}_	ext{w}$), and the energy density $\epsilon$.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the spectral edge ($\epsilon 	o 0^+$) versus the spectral bulk, and compares integrable versus non-integrable regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on identifying and excluding 'outlier states' whose presence distorts the scaling laws, and for the 2D case, assumes local fluxes can be approximately conserved.
figures_summary: Figures show GOE behavior in gap ratios for non-integrable models, volume-law growth of EE near the spectral edge, and finite-size scaling consistent with ETH for local observable fluctuations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework concerning EMICQ and ETH breakdown. It then applies this framework to specific 1D and 2D spin models, using spectral diagnostics (gap ratios, EE scaling) to confirm the persistence of thermalization near the spectral edge.
why_interesting: The finding that incompatible symmetries can sustain thermalization deep into the spectral edge provides a powerful theoretical mechanism for understanding quantum thermalization in complex, highly constrained quantum materials.
